bibliography.abstract: Prevailing narratives on urban conservation in Egypt begin with Historic Cairo's inscription on UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1979. However, its emergence as a distinctive approach can be traced to the 1920s-1930s when French Architect Edmond Pauty developed his proposal “La défense de l'ancienne ville du Caire et de ses monuments. Urbanisme et archéologie” while working as Architecte-Expert at the Comité de Conservation des Monuments de l'Art Arabe in Egypt. Pauty's Cairo proposal drew on his prior experience as director of historic monuments in Morocco, where he had first formulated his ideas on safeguarding historic cities, representing a fascinating case of knowledge transfer from one colonial context to another. His approach marked a departure from the prevailing focus on individual monuments to encompass entire historic cities --an avant-garde concept predating key international developments in the field. Pauty's innovative plan remained largely unimplemented and faced resistance from Egyptian Comité members, reflecting growing tensions between foreign and Egyptian expertise amidst rising nationalism. Drawing from Pauty's published work and archival material, I examine his contribution to the emergence of urban conservation in Egypt and its intersections with colonial and nationalist dynamics, situating his work within broader transnational narratives of conservation and planning history.
bibliography.title: Beyond monuments: Edmond Pauty's vision for Historic Cairo in early twentieth century Egypt

en.caveats: The analysis is historical and qualitative, focusing on a single, largely unimplemented planning proposal and its associated archival records.
en.what: This study analyzes Edmond Pauty's unimplemented 1920s-1930s proposal for Historic Cairo, tracing how he adapted urban conservation concepts from his prior work in colonial Morocco. Using Pauty's published writings and archival documents, the research details how his plan shifted focus from isolated monuments to the preservation of entire historic urban fabrics, and documents the resistance he faced from Egyptian committee members amid rising nationalist sentiment.
en.why: The research pushes back the origins of urban-scale conservation in Egypt by fifty years, demonstrating that holistic historic district planning was conceptualized in the region long before its formalization by UNESCO in 1979.
